newsitem.title: USA: Duke says N.C. McGuire 1 nuke in restart.
newsitem.headline: Duke says N.C. McGuire 1 nuke in restart.

text.p: Duke Power Co said Thursday it has begun the restart process at its 1,129 megawatt (MW) McGuire 1 nuclear power plant in Cornelius, N.C., and expects the unit to be back on the grid sometime this weekend.
The unit was shut Oct 31 after one of the facility's four backup battery banks failed to meet performance criteria during a recent test.
The outage shut the adjacent McGuire 2 unit as well. It is also rated at 1,129 MW.
A company spokeswoman said unit 2 would likely resume power production one day after unit 1 was back on line.
Duke had originally said on Oct 31 it expected the two McGuire units to be out of service for at least three weeks.
"We hope (unit 1) will be back on line sometime this weekend, if not early next week," spokeswoman Guynn Savage said Thursday, adding the startup of units 1 and 2 "should be about one day apart."
Duke's Oconee nuclear facility in Seneca, S.C., has also been shut following a steam pipe rupture in September that injured seven employees.
The three Oconee power units produce a combined total of 2,538 MW of electricity.
No restart date has been set for the Oconee units, although the company has said it will not meet original expectations of having two of the units on line by mid-November.
